# ECON 0100 | Exercise E4 | Duopoly

*Exercises are a certificate of the work done together in class and offers extra practice outside class.*

Flue networks forms a convenient form of communication and transportation for those in the wizarding world. Its easy to move between flue portals on the network or use it to chat with those at a distance. Due to the benefits of adding *to* an existing network instead of starting a new one (i.e. network effects) there have historically only been two networks: Fast Flue Inc. and Soot Net. The demand for flue network trips is $P = 120 - Q$, and any network’s marginal cost is $MC = 2q$. The networks use a sophisticated ticketing system to charge a price for every trip. Prices are in galleons.

### Warmup | One Flue Network

The history of flue networks started with Fast Flue Inc. At one point they were the only network. They had a marginal revenue of $MR = 120 - 2Q$.

a\) As a monopolist how many trips would Fast Flue Inc. sell?\
b\) What price would they charge per trip?

 

 

### Q1 | A Second Network

Today, after Soot Net joined the market, both networks sell into the same market, so the demand is $P = 120 - (q_F + q_S)$ and Fast Flue Inc.’s marginal revenue is $MR_F = 120 - 2q_F - q_S$.

a\) What is Fast Flue Inc.’s Best Response?\
b\) If Soot Net sells 40 trips, how many trips does Fast Flue Inc. choose to sell?

 

 

 

### Q2 | Duopoly Equilibrium

The best responses of the two networks are below. This market is symmetric.

:::: {.columns gutter=1em}

::: {.column width=60%}

$$
BR_F: q_F = 30 - \tfrac{1}{4} q_S
$$

$$
BR_S: q_S = 30 - \tfrac{1}{4} q_F
$$

a\) What is the Nash equilibrium quantity?\
b\) What is the market price at this equilibrium?\
c\) What profit does Fast Flue Inc. make in equilibrium? Its average total cost at this quantity is 61.5 galleons.

:::

### Q3 | Is It Efficient?

:::: {.columns gutter=1em}

::: {.column width=60%}

With two networks the price of a trip is 72 galleons, and each network’s marginal cost at 24 trips is 48 galleons. There are no externalities. Is this outcome efficient?
